comments.value: At this point it doesn't seem like security is a big concern for the VRChat team. They didn't address security in any significant way during the IL2CPP update where they would've had the perfect opportunity to do so, and I've personally seen them unban users who were actively selling modified clients despite knowing their malicious history.

I can’t say anything about the moderation or moderation team, but I was there with this dev much of the night and he dealt with a lot of others earlier and obviously was tired of dealing with it while he was trying to enjoy his evening. I don’t blame him for his response at all. Having a short clip like that out of context is not very helpful.

@{5ba582b58c7e6b41cd563bf6|full_name}: Sounds like they need to hire some dedicated moderators then, so people don't need to ask random devs to remove script kiddies. Hire some moderators, bring back the 'request moderator' button to players who aren't visitor status, and have the ability take the button away from anyone who misuses it.

I jump worlds a fair bit, on one hand people openly talking about ripping models or using clients in void clubs (around 70% of the time). Kinda hard to not notice/ walk into it.
Then on the other hand , i see people on half-naked children looking models, this happens in public worlds. This keeps me away from the game more than anything else.
no matter how many reports get sent, i just see the same people doing it, nothing happens they just continue going around on those models exposing themselves to adults and children alike. 
-also real reports sent via website not the in game button click- 
I guess it just bothers me that there's real issues that need attention, that never get touched.
that video shows how they're corrupt. third world in a nutshell

@{5bafbca9282d5d55fb6899f8|full_name}: Might want to limit that player status to at least "trusted." There are tons of people not within the "visitor" status that would have that ability. Thousands of people misuse 911 today in the real world. With how chaotic the player base is in VRChat, I believe the moderators would have a mass intake of requests. 
Then they would have to black-list all of those people who misuse it. That alone would take probably, what, months?
Back then, it was perfectly fine because there were only about a couple hundred people on VRChat at the same time. The community was so tiny it was manageable.
On the other hand, I have heard many rumors from a few of my friends and other people about the moderators not doing their job for legit reasons, such as 753, whoever that is down there V-V-V...  
I've never known about any mods that do this, nor have I heard of this until as of recently, but If that is the case, it needs to be dealt with.

@{5b77e1e0c11e8156cccde685|full_name}: I agree. There are a lot of people that do this in public worlds. I don't blame you for avoiding the game because of this. It really does seem that there is not enough moderation staff to keep worlds in check. I often wonder how many people they have.

I'm a regular player who's quiet, never has drama & gets along with many users yet I'm randomly banned twice for very small reasons (currently 1 monthed now infact). Messaging support with straight to the point appeals got me nowhere. I do not use NSFW/client/harm any users, I simply want to spend time around my wonderful friends & upload avatars which I keep as optimised as possible since I don't like causing hassle. Feel like I am asking for too much though

This post is not appropriate for the VRChat Feedback boards. The VRChat Team does not consist solely of moderators. As noted in our Community Guidelines: **"When encountering a VRChat employee in the app, please keep in mind that even employees come in to relax and hang out with the community. Please respect their free time and treat them as you would other community members."**
VRChat Moderators will never be visible in the application, and will only communicate with VRChat players via the Moderation ticket system. They will _never_ contact users in the application or via any other method.
All communications regarding the Moderation team or Moderation in VRChat must be submitted via our Moderation help form.
[Contact our Moderation team](http://help.vrchat.com/new) (and select the "MOD" category) to request information regarding moderation, or to submit a moderation report.
@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: Way to completely skirt around the problem of people being banned for nothing and your terrible TOS causing more issues than it fixes.

@{5f120ddd754bc479b07702d7|full_name}: What's funny is I've already contacted via moderation help form. I'm being patient as ever about my ban & have nothing bad to say. Just asking for a reconsider to unban. Even a "no" will be fine since it's an actual response
@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: i wish i could wear my work uniform at work and call it free time
@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: It's a convenient way to do things, so VRChat can have no moderation and just say "They're in there, just trust us, OK?"

@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: Does that actually work or is that just to waste peoples time until they give up? It says you'll get back to us within 24 business hours but it took 2 months for me to get an automated "ban appeal denied" email. I've seen quite a few people banned for ridiculous reasons like ban evasion on their main account but I've never seen anyone get anything but the automated response. Even if your email isn't a ban appeal, if the title has ban in it you're going to get a "we read your email and due to overwhelming proof your appeal is denied." If they actually read the email they'd know it wasn't a ban appeal.
What actually does work, instead of contacting their moderation team, is personally messaging VRChat staff over Discord. I've seen that work more often than I've seen someone get anything resolved through email.

details:
The VRChat moderation team (this includes members of the VRChat team) never has been the greatest but it feels as though it has been degrading over time.
Someone could be violating terms of service in the same lobby as them and 90% of them wont care and or wont do anything about it.
I've met several people have been banned for no reason and/or were banned from something like ban evasion when they've only ever had one account their entire time on VRChat.
I'm sure some of you people reading this right now have fallen victim to things like this.
If you'd like to see an example of how great the team is currently, here is a small clip for your viewing pleasure.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tKg1GhK5ev0
Regardless of your position in the team, you should care about what goes on in the game especially if its happening in the same lobby as you.
I'm not directly asking for a new moderation team but maybe just maybe things could be stepped up a bit.
Your friend,
Odds
title: Request for better VRChat staff/moderators
